question.text: Consider the function $L: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by $L(\mathbf{x}) = (\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b})^T(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b})$ where \[ \mathbf{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}. \] What is $\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L(\mathbf{x})$ at $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
We can solve this problem by applying the chain rule for gradients.

Let $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}.$ Then, $L(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{y}^T\mathbf{y},$ and

\[ \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L = \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}L}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}}\right)^T = \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}}\right)^T \cdot \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}L}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}\right)^T. \]

Now, since

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}\left(\mathbf{y}^T\mathbf{y}\right) = 2\mathbf{y}^T \qquad\text{and}\qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}} = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}} (\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}) = \mathbf{A}, \]

we have that

\begin{align*} \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L &= \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}}\right)^T \cdot \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}L}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}\right)^T \\[5pt] &= \mathbf{A}^T \cdot 2\mathbf{y}. \end{align*}

Evaluating at $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$, we get

\begin{align*} \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L &= \mathbf{A}^T \cdot 2\mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot \mathbf{A}^T (\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}) \\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}^T \left(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\right) \\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \left(\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\right) \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 8 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 52 \\ -8 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the function $L: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by $L(\mathbf{x}) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}\right)^T \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}\right)$ where \[ \mathbf{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \] What is $\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L(\mathbf{x})$ at $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
We can solve this problem by applying the chain rule for gradients.

Let $\mathbf{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}.$ Then, $L(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{y}^T\mathbf{y},$ and

\[ \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L = \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}L}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}}\right)^T = \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}}\right)^T \cdot \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}L}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}\right)^T. \]

Now, since

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}\left(\mathbf{y}^T\mathbf{y}\right) = 2\mathbf{y}^T \qquad\text{and}\qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}} = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}, \]

we have that

\begin{align*} \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L &= \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{x}}\right)^T \cdot \left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}L}{\textrm{d}\mathbf{y}}\right)^T \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\right)^T \cdot 2\mathbf{y}. \end{align*}

Evaluating at $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$, we get

\begin{align*} \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} L & = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\right)^T \cdot 2\mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= \mathbf{A}^T \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b}\right) \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}^T \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\right) \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 16 \\ 34 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\right) \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \left(\begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 17 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\right) \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 14 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 62 \\ 45 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}
